summary: Requests between members of an organization: one record with an addressee, a project, a deadline, a thread and an append-only trail, and the /org/{orgId}/requests page turned from a manager-only vacation feed into everyone's inbox. The branch already carries an implementation of this spec (commits 481a165 and 6f2dbb5) and the additive migration 20260901140000_requests_01_requests is in the preflight baseline; ffa814d then amended the spec in the human's answer to two spec blockers review raised. So this is not a green field. The work is the delta: the decline path writes a RequestMessage with no message_posted event, four web capability checks pass the raw Membership.role into can() which does not normalize, @ds has no multiline text control while three raw <textarea> elements are hand-styled, the detail screen swallows every load error that is not a 404, and four E2E assertions either cannot fail or do not follow the steps the spec names. Each task below says what already exists at which path and what the delta on it is; do not rewrite what is there.

tasks.title: Create path: validation, per-organization number, org scoping — verify against the spec and fix the description validator

migration.note: No new migration. Requests spec 01's migration is already applied as 20260901140000_requests_01_requests and is in the preflight baseline; one migration per run means this run adds none. If anything here forces a schema change, it must stay additive, because infra/deploy.sh:175-190 registers the migrate task definition, runs infra/migrate.sh, and only then tf applies the services at :187 — the schema is live while the previous image is still serving.

concurrency.lock: SELECT "nextRequestNumber" FROM "Organization" WHERE "id" = $1 FOR UPDATE, already at requests.service.ts:355-358, inside the same $transaction as the Request insert and the created event

tasks.notes: Exists and is correct: the FOR UPDATE allocation (:353-361), the created event in the same transaction (requirement 11), the 404-for-a-cross-organization project or membership versus 400 projectUnavailable / assigneeInactive for an in-organization one (requirements 9 and 13, edge cases 18a and 7), and assigneeKind = 'member' as the only accepted value (requirement 12). The one delta: packages/validation/src/requests.ts#validateRequestDescription reports a non-string description as descriptionTooLong, a message that names a different failure. Validation rule 2 gives no key for a malformed value, so coerce a non-string to null rather than inventing a message — the rendered form cannot produce the input and the Error Messages table must not gain a key the spec does not name. Do not touch the numbering, the locks, or the 404/400 split.

tasks.title: The thread and its audit trail: write the message_posted event on the decline path

migration.note: No schema change. RequestEvent already carries action, actorMembershipId and newLabel (schema.prisma:1152-1174); this task writes one more row of an existing shape.

concurrency.lock: the decline branch already runs inside transition()'s $transaction after lockRequest() takes SELECT … FROM "Request" … FOR UPDATE (requests.service.ts:778-792); the new event is written in that same transaction, never after it

tasks.notes: Requirement 19 is unconditional — 'Every message writes a RequestEvent with action = message_posted in the same transaction as the RequestMessage row'. There are exactly two RequestMessage call sites. postMessage (:438-465) writes the event and bumps lastActivityAt; the decline branch (:522-529) writes the message and no event. Requirement 25 makes the decline reason a RequestMessage, so requirement 19 governs it. This does not breach state-machine invariant 4, which counts status_changed events only: a declined request ends with one message_posted and one status_changed. Snapshot the author's display name into newLabel exactly as postMessage does (requirement 20), so the thread and history survive the author's removal. Extend TC-01-INT-11 to assert both events; do not add a case id the spec does not name. Requirement 17 stays scoped to the POST …/messages endpoint, as its own sentence scopes it — the decline's message is written while the locked row is still non-terminal and that is not a violation.

tasks.title: Lifecycle: keep the locked guards intact, and stop reassignment writing a no-op event

migration.note: No schema change. answeredAt, resolvedAt and resolvedByAccountId are already nullable columns of the applied migration; the deploy order that made them safe is infra/deploy.sh:183-190, migrate then tf apply.

concurrency.lock: SELECT "id", "status", "requesterMembershipId", "assigneeMembershipId", "answeredAt", "resolvedAt" FROM "Request" WHERE "id" = $1 AND "organizationId" = $2 FOR UPDATE (requests.service.ts#lockRequest, :783-789), taken by every one of the three writers above

tasks.notes: Authorization work: every actor guard here runs against normalizeRole() via requireCaller (requests.service.ts:846), which is what makes the matrix hold against today's admin/member data — do not replace it with a raw role read. Exists and is correct: the terminal guard before the transition guard (409 alreadyTerminal, then 409 invalidTransition, then 403 notYoursTo*), the party-versus-non-party split that gives a party 403 and a non-party 404 (requirement 23, edge case 4a, AC-16), write-once answeredAt/resolvedAt (requirement 31), and the five editable fields with a field_changed event each and no-op suppression (requirement 34, :626-656). Requirement 36 no longer names a reassignment filter — ffa814d removed that clause — so add none; the banner is the mechanism. The one delta: reassignRequest (:686-763) makes no comparison against locked.assigneeMembershipId, so reassigning to the member who already holds the request writes an assignee_changed event whose oldValue equals its newValue and moves lastActivityAt, reordering the row under requirement 43. Mirror patchRequest's no-op suppression and return the row unchanged. Also update the comment above TC-01-INT-13 in apps/api/test/requests.spec.ts:691-701: it argues against the spec's old steps, which ffa814d replaced with the two routes that test already takes, and a comment arguing an exception to text that no longer says it will be read as a live dissent.

tasks.title: List endpoint: scope, the retired vocabulary, the two unfiltered counters and the default order

migration.note: No schema change — this is a read path. VacationRequest gains no column and no write; only its read query gains requirement 42's status mapping.

concurrency.lock: none — every path here is a read. The two counters are separate count() queries issued before the filters are applied (requests.service.ts:203-213) and are deliberately not a count of the returned array; do not fold them into the findMany.

tasks.notes: Requirement 33 is the 'every read' rule and the six call sites above are its complete list — overdue is derived per reading account from Account.timezone (schema.prisma:37) at each of them and stored nowhere. Exists and is correct: 400 on an unknown status or type rather than the retired fallback to pending (requirement 42, AC-17), the fixed open→pending / granted→approved / declined→rejected / answered→none mapping (vacationStatusesFor), type=vacation as a choice of section, waitingOnMe and total computed before the filters, vacation.pendingCount always the unfiltered pending count, the vacation block present only for a view-requests holder, and compareRequestRows putting non-terminal before terminal as the first key (requirement 43). The delta: vacation-request-feed.service.ts#countAll (:123) has no caller anywhere in apps/ or packages/ — it is the lifted totalCount of the retired spec-10 envelope, which is now { requests, pendingCount }. Delete it. Note for the record and do not change: listRequests also answers 400 for an unknown scope (:175), which the spec's GET Errors list names for status and type only; it is stricter than the spec rather than looser and is recorded as a risk.

tasks.title: Web: every capability check this feature added runs through normalizeRole()

migration.note: No schema change; this task is client-side authorization only. A web-only deploy skips the migration step entirely (infra/deploy.sh:175).

allCallSites: apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/requests/page.tsx:87-90 — role cast, then can(role,'create-request'), can(role,'view-all-requests'), can(role,'list-assigned-projects')
apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/requests/[requestId]/page.tsx:46-48 — role cast, then can(role,'view-all-requests') and role === 'admin'
apps/web/src/layout/Sidebar.tsx:82-90 — the Requests row, deliberately unconditional (requirement 38) and taking no capability check
tasks.notes: This task touches authorization, so it must name normalizeRole() (packages/validation/src/roles.ts): the database holds admin/member while the spec's matrix is admin|manager|user|viewer, and the spec's Roles & Permission Matrix states 'Capability checks run against normalizeRole(), so the legacy member value maps to user and the matrix holds against today's data'. can() at packages/validation/src/index.ts:716 reads CAPABILITY_MATRIX[role] directly and does not normalize, so a legacy member resolves to undefined and gets every capability denied — the New Request control disappears for a role the server grants create-request to (requirement 1). Wrap each call site above as can(normalizeRole(session.role), …). Normalize at these call sites, not inside can(): can() is read by clients, members, projects and time-tracking screens as well and changing it moves those without a spec. The detail screen's role === 'admin' comparison must normalize too. Sidebar's Requests row stays unconditional — that is requirement 38, and it is what makes the 'no dead links' rule hold, since every role can now reach the destination. Requirement 41's vacation section is server-decided (the vacation key is absent for a non-holder), and the client must keep rendering the section only when the key is present rather than deciding it itself.

tasks.title: Web screens: the row, the flags, the two empty states, and a load-error state on the detail screen

migration.note: No schema change; web only, and a web-only deploy runs no migration (infra/deploy.sh:175).

allCallSites: apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/requests/page.tsx:368-395 — the list's error banner and retry
tasks.notes: Exists and is correct: the row's number, title, status, addressee, project and the two flags (requirement 45); requests-empty-state carrying emptyMine unfiltered and emptyFiltered with filters (requirement 46); the list's requests-error-banner with requests-error-retry-btn keeping the last good rows behind it. Two deltas. (a) The detail screen's load() (:61-76) sets notFound only for a 404 and swallows everything else, so a 500 or a thrown fetch leaves request-detail-page containing a back link and nothing else, indefinitely, with no message and no retry — the list screen was given a banner for exactly this. Track a load error alongside notFound and render the same banner-and-retry shape, reusing REQUEST_MESSAGES.genericError, which is what the list already renders (page.tsx:385). Do not invent copy and do not write it inline. (b) RequestHistory.tsx:20 reads `event.actor.displayName ?? event.newLabel ?? 'Former member'`, so an assignee_changed row whose actorMembershipId was SetNull renders the new addressee as the person who did the reassigning. Fall back to 'Former member' directly for the actor, and read newLabel as the actor only where the event's own semantics define it that way — message_posted's author snapshot, requirement 20.

The three raw <textarea> elements above are each hand-styled with a literal 12px mixed into a token-valued padding, which is the improvisation CLAUDE.md forbids: anything missing goes into the design system, never per screen. Add the control to the design system, export it through the @ds barrel and apps/web/src/ds.ts, and use it at all three call sites — all three, not one, or the next screen copies whichever was left. Keep every existing data-testid on the rendered element: request-new-description, request-detail-composer and request-detail-decline-reason are named in the spec's Required data-testid list and are queried by TC-01-E2E-01, -02 and -05. tasks.title: E2E: make the four assertions that cannot fail, or that skip the steps, able to fail

migration.note: No schema change; tests only. A change under e2e/ ships in no image and deploys nothing (deploy.yml).

allCallSites: e2e/tests/requests.spec.ts TC-01-E2E-11 — the closing sidebar-requests-badge absence assertion
e2e/tests/requests.spec.ts TC-01-E2E-08 — the `user` half's requests-vacation-section absence assertion
e2e/tests/requests.spec.ts TC-01-E2E-05 — the empty decline reason
tasks.notes: Run these targeted, never the whole suite: from e2e, E2E_WEB_PORT=3100 E2E_API_PORT=4100 CI=1 npx playwright test tests/requests.spec.ts tests/regressions.spec.ts. Four fixes. (a) TC-01-E2E-11: after the final reload, the badge node is absent before the GET it depends on resolves — Sidebar renders it only when badgeCount is truthy and requests-badge-context.tsx initialises it to 0 — so toHaveCount(0) passes on its first poll and would pass even if the server returned waitingOnMe: 2. Anchor on the response (waitForResponse on the list call, or assert a post-response node first) before asserting absence. The spec calls this case the regression witness for requirement 44, so it has to be able to fail. (b) TC-01-E2E-08: openRequestsPage waits only for requests-page, the outer div drawn before any fetch, while requests-vacation-section is drawn only from data.vacation — the `user` half's absence assertion therefore passes while the list request is still in flight. Wait for something only the response can draw (the empty state, or a seeded row) before asserting the section is absent; this is the only level that observes the UI half of AC-2 and AC-3. The requests-scope-toggle assertion in the same case is sound and needs no change — it renders synchronously from the session. (c) TC-01-E2E-05: the spec's expected result is 'shows the field error and changes no status'; the test asserts only that the reason textarea is still visible. Assert the 'changes no status' half against request-detail-status, which is a spec-named id. Do not invent a testid for the decline error node — CLAUDE.md permits data-testid selectors only and the ids are named in the specs, so that assertion waits on note P2. (d) TC-01-E2E-13: the spec's steps say to clear the filter and its selector list names requests-type-filter, which no test in e2e/ queries; the case switches accounts instead, leaving the Clear-filters control (page.tsx:416) with no coverage at any level. Clear the filter as the steps say. While in this file, TC-01-E2E-01 binds admin and then asserts only admin.id.length > 0 — use it for what it was fetched for, the created row's addressee, or drop both.

risks.risk: The branch already contains an implementation of this spec, so an implementer who reads the plan as a green field will rewrite working code and lose the review's accepted parts.
risks.mitigation: Every task names the file and the line of what exists and states its delta in one sentence. Nothing in this plan asks for a new module, a new table or a new route.

risks.risk: Fixing the role normalization inside can() rather than at the call sites would silently move the clients, members, projects and time-tracking screens, none of which is in this spec.

risks.risk: listRequests answers 400 for an unknown scope, which the spec's GET Errors list names for status and type only. It is stricter than the spec rather than looser, and no case pins it either way.
risks.mitigation: Recorded here rather than changed. Removing it would make a hand-edited scope fall back silently, which is the failure mode requirement 42 rejects for the sibling parameters. The spec should gain the row.

risks.risk: T2 adds a second RequestEvent to the decline transaction, and a case asserting 'exactly one event' on that path would start failing.
